Let’s dive into Chapter 7: “Cultivating a Dominant Mindset—Thinking Like a Leader.”
Have you ever noticed how some people just seem to expect to win, even when things look uncertain? That’s not arrogance—it’s about building a mindset where you believe you have the power to make things happen.
When we talk about a dominant mindset, we’re not talking about being overbearing. Instead, it’s about taking responsibility for your path, looking at challenges as chances to grow, and seeing setbacks as just a temporary detour.
So, how do you actually develop this kind of thinking? Let’s break down a few key habits:
First, assume control. No matter what’s going on, approach every situation as if you can influence the outcome—even when the odds feel stacked against you. It’s about refusing to be a bystander in your own life.
Next, don’t just compete for scraps. Instead of fighting over what’s left, ask yourself—what if you could create a whole new opportunity, or even change the rules of the game? Think bigger and look for ways to expand the pie, not just grab a slice.
Another important piece is acting with urgency. Treat your goals as if they’re non-negotiable. When you act like there’s no time to waste, you’ll find yourself moving faster and with more intention.
And don’t forget to visualize your success. Take a few moments each day to really picture yourself crushing those 10X goals. See it, feel it, and let that vision fuel your confidence and motivation.
Here’s a helpful way to look at it: Imagine you’re a chess player, always thinking several moves ahead. You’re not just reacting to what’s happening—you’re shaping the board, setting yourself up to win in the long run. In business, that might mean launching something bold and new instead of just copying what everyone else is doing. And in your personal life, it could look like setting clear boundaries to protect your time and energy.
The real heart of a dominant mindset is this: Own your outcomes—good or bad. Don’t wait around for perfect conditions or someone’s permission. Leaders create momentum by taking decisive action, and that energy inspires everyone around them. It also tends to attract new opportunities that would stay hidden otherwise.
So, if you want to sustain big, 10X action, start by thinking like a leader—confident, responsible, and always ready to shape your own future.
